title: Structs, Enums and Arrays in a Packet-Decoder Bench
description: Give a packet decoder's flat ports names and meaning: typedef enums with a 4-state base, packed structs for the header and the decoder's answer, a dynamic array of stimulus grown with new[N](old), and associative-array traffic tables checked key by key. The bench predicts every result from the specification, compares with !==, prints one PASS/FAIL line and is proven to fail on planted DUT and bench bugs.

steps.title: Step 1: Read the specification and run the starter
steps.instructions: Read the pkt_decoder specification in the README (header layout and rules D1 to D5). Compile work/pkt_pkg.sv, work/pkt_decoder.sv and work/tb_top.sv in that order and run tb_top. It prints TEST 0 packets and PASS=0 FAIL=0. Before you open the README's answer, explain why that line is not a pass.

steps.title: Step 2: Write the types
steps.instructions: In work/pkt_pkg.sv, replace the four placeholders: kind_e as typedef enum logic [2:0] {K_IDLE = 3'd0, K_READ = 3'd1, K_WRITE = 3'd2, K_RESP = 3'd4}; err_e as typedef enum logic [1:0] {E_NONE, E_KIND, E_CHK, E_LEN}; hdr_t as a packed struct of kind_e kind, logic [3:0] dest, logic [4:0] len and logic [3:0] chk; dec_t as a packed struct of logic accept, err_e err, logic [3:0] dest and logic [4:0] len. Then delete the /* and */ lines in check_types() in work/tb_top.sv and rerun: no TYPES fatal. Answer the README's question on swapping dest and len.

steps.title: Step 3: The reference model
steps.instructions: Write the bodies of hdr_chk (D2: XOR of h[15:12], h[11:8] and h[7:4]), kind_is_member ($cast called as a function into a kind_e), make_hdr (an assignment pattern by member name, then the checksum), raw_hdr (the whole struct from the concatenation {kind, d, l, 4'h0}, then a right or wrong checksum) and model_decode (err in D3's priority order, accept from D4, dest and len from D5). Write them from the specification, not from the RTL. Then explain why raw_hdr can put kind 5 into the struct when h.kind = 3'd5; does not compile.

steps.title: Step 4: The stimulus list
steps.instructions: Fill in build_stimulus from the README's plan table: stim = new[6]; entries 0 to 5 with make_hdr; then stim = new[stim.size() + 4](stim); so the first six survive; entries 6, 7 and 8 with raw_hdr and entry 9 with make_hdr. Rerun: TEST 10 packets, and still PASS=0 FAIL=0. Name the row that tests the order of D3, and the two rows that test the length limit.

steps.title: Step 5: The per-packet check
steps.instructions: Write dec_str with $sformatf and d.err.name(). Write check_packet: act = {accept, err, dest, len}; exp = model_decode(h); seen_err[exp.err]++; compare act !== exp and count pass_cnt or fail_cnt with an $error that prints both; add exp.len to exp_bytes[exp.dest] when the model accepts, and act.len to act_bytes[act.dest] plus count_by_kind[h.kind]++ when act.accept === 1'b1. Rerun: PASS=10 FAIL=0.

steps.title: Step 6: Tables, plan and verdict
steps.instructions: Write print_traffic (walk count_by_kind with first() and next(); foreach over exp_bytes), compare_tables (every key of exp_bytes must exist in act_bytes with the same value, and every key of act_bytes must exist in exp_bytes; call exists() before reading the other table), check_plan (walk err_e from first() to last() with next() and fail for each member that seen_err does not contain) and, in report, count a run that checked nothing as a failure. Run with DUT_BUG = 0 and expect the README's log, ending PASS=17 FAIL=0.

steps.title: Step 7: Break the DUT and the bench, and watch the checks catch it
steps.instructions: Predict, then run: DUT_BUG = 1 (length limit off by one), DUT_BUG = 2 (checksum checked before kind) and DUT_BUG = 3 (dest from the wrong bits). Then plant your own DUT bug, accept = (err == 2'd0); so IDLE is accepted, and a bench bug, new[stim.size() + 4] without (stim). Compare each summary line and the check that caught it with the README's table, then undo everything and rerun: PASS=17 FAIL=0.
